title: Copyright complaints to Google against Maltese websites covering the state hospitals privatisation deal
exclusion_reason: Senders not identified (complaints filed under different names or pseudonyms), and individual target outlets, notices and outcomes are not documented case by case; kept as European-target context alongside Part 3.3 of the report
summary: In May 2024 Times of Malta reported that scores of copyright complaints targeting Maltese websites were filed with Google from March 2024, weeks before a magisterial inquiry into the privatisation of three state hospitals concluded; in April 2024 former Prime Minister Joseph Muscat and two other former senior officials were charged in connection with the deal. Megan Mallia, a University of Malta researcher writing for EDMO/MedDMO (January 2025), found that one blog post alone received at least five complaints, each filed under a different name or pseudonym in close succession and each claiming that the post had copied a different article. Searches combining Maltese news sites and blogs with "ram tumuluri" or "vitals global healthcare" (September 2024) returned Google notices that results had been removed following copyright complaints. Who filed the complaints has not been established.
